extracted.intended_audience: patent owners and patent practitioners preparing or filing requests for supplemental examination with the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for preparing, filing, and prosecuting a request for supplemental examination under 35 U.S.C. 257 and 37 CFR 1.610, including content, formatting, filing-date, correction, and prosecution limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed explanation requirement (37 CFR 1.610(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a detailed explanation of how each item of information submitted may be applied to each claim for which supplemental examination is requested (per 37 CFR 1.610(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners are encouraged to be as comprehensive as possible so the owner can frame potential issues and assist the examiner in focusing the review. Failure to provide the required explanation for any item of information or for any claim will be identified in a Notice of Noncompliant Supplemental Examination Request. Even if not strictly compliant, the Office may accept the request if it is readily understood how items may be applied to claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements are not admissions of unpatentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements in the detailed explanation will NOT be construed as an admission of unpatentability; they indicate that the patent owner is requesting the Office consider whether certain issues may be raised by each item of information with respect to specific claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners may identify specific patentability issues (e.g., anticipation, obviousness, written description, enablement) in the explanation to provide focused review and explicit consideration of potential issues on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request must stand on its own; no incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed explanation requirement cannot be met by incorporating by reference a paper from another proceeding or by relying on a paper of a third party; a request for supplemental examination must stand on its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent owner wishes the examiner to consider an Office action from another proceeding, that Office action and any documents mentioned must be separately listed as items of information under 37 CFR 1.610(b)(2), copies provided when required, and the patent owner must supply its own detailed explanation under 37 CFR 1.610(b)(5) of how those documents may be applied to the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed explanation must reflect patent owner's opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed explanation must reflect the opinion of the patent owner and not that of a third party (including a patent examiner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute does not authorize another party to file a request on behalf of the patent owner. The patent owner may not rely on papers drafted by third parties to satisfy 37 CFR 1.610(b)(5) because they may not reflect the patent owner's views on relevance and application to each claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of factual information requires additional supporting items
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request includes an item of information limited to correction of factual information (e.g., foreign priority or domestic benefit claim, common ownership), the request should also include one or more additional items of information that potentially show the patentability of the claims depends on the factual information to be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: To correct an effective filing date by claiming benefit of a parent patent, include the parent patent and an intervening reference, and explain how the intervening reference may be applied to the claims if the effective filing date remains unchanged, and explain how the patent owner is entitled to the corrected factual information (e.g., how each claim limitation is supported by the parent). If merely deleting a benefit/priority claim, an explanation of entitlement to a new effective filing date may not be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional content permitted under 37 CFR 1.610(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request may optionally include: (1) a cover sheet itemizing each component submitted; (2) a table of contents; (3) an explanation of how the claims patentably distinguish over the items of information; and (4) an explanation of why each item does or does not raise a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of optional items (cover sheet, table of contents) is encouraged to assist Office review (use of form PTO/SB/59 is particularly encouraged). Optional discussions under (c)(3) and (c)(4) should be presented separately from the required detailed explanation (under distinct subheadings) to avoid the risk that the required explanation is not found in compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not combine optional patentability-argument with required detailed explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests that combine the detailed explanation under 37 CFR 1.610(b)(5) with the optional discussion under 37 CFR 1.610(c)(3) often have lengthy patentability arguments with little explanation of how items apply to claim limitations, risking a finding of noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner submits the optional content, the Office strongly recommends presenting it under separate subheadings (e.g., 'Optional Explanation under 37 CFR 1.610(c)(3)'). Combining discussions can cause the Office to find the required explanation was not provided and lose the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet (ADS) under 37 CFR 1.76 cannot be submitted in a supplemental examination proceeding because such a proceeding is not an 'application.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include ADS in supplemental examination filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date prerequisites and Office discretion (37 CFR 1.610(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a request for supplemental examination will not be granted if the request is not in compliance with §§ 1.605, 1.615, and 1.610, subject to the discretion of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not entitled to a filing date, the patent owner will be notified and given an opportunity to complete the request within a specified time. If timely corrected, the receipt date of the corrected request becomes the filing date. The Office may grant a filing date to a defective request at its discretion, generally only for minor defects (e.g., formatting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Noncompliant Supplemental Examination Request and correction opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office determines the original request is not entitled to a filing date, the Central Reexamination Unit will mail a Notice of Noncompliant Supplemental Examination Request detailing defects and provide a specified time (generally 15 days) to timely file a corrected request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner does not timely comply, the request will not be granted a filing date and the reexamination fee will be refunded. The notice will specify defects and may include an attachment explaining noncompliance with filing date requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected request must be complete and replace original
rubrics_metrics.description: A corrected request must include all components the patent owner intends to include and must replace the originally filed request; do not submit only a supplemental or partial corrected portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office intends to expunge the entire originally-filed request once a corrected request is received. Corrected request must contain all required information without reliance on the defective original. Fees already paid do not need to be resubmitted. Corrected requests may be filed electronically or by mail but must not be faxed. Patent owner has one opportunity to file a corrected request in response to the Notice of Noncompliant Request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may sua sponte correct minor defects in corrected requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a corrected request contains only minor defects, the Office may in its discretion enter the defective corrected request, correct the defects sua sponte, and/or request a submission to correct the defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: omission of a copy of the patent in the corrected request where the copy was present in the original submission — the Office may accept the original submission as part of the corrected request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination for failure to timely or properly correct
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper corrected request is not timely filed, or if the corrected request is defective/improper, the request will not be granted a filing date and processing will be terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single failure to comply ordinarily results in loss of filing date; upon termination the Office will mail a Notice of Termination, refund reexamination fee if paid, retain the control number but not grant a filing date, and the request papers will remain unavailable to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited set of actions while supplemental examination pending
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing a request for supplemental examination, the only Office actions relevant to the supplemental examination are: (1) determination whether the request is entitled to a filing date; and (2) determination whether any submitted items raise a SNQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may hold in abeyance action on any petition or other paper until after issuance of the supplemental examination certificate to assist in making the SNQ determination within the three-month statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of papers other than the request
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing a request, no papers other than (1) a corrected request responding to a Notice of Noncompliant Request, or (2) a notice of a prior or concurrent post-patent Office proceeding under 37 CFR 1.620(d), should be filed prior to conclusion of the supplemental examination; other papers will not be entered and may be discarded or expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an unauthorized paper is entered inadvertently, it may be expunged from the record (marked 'non-public' and 'closed'). A copy of the Office communication notifying the patent owner of the return/expungement will be made of record; no copy of the returned/expunged paper will be retained by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party papers prohibited (35 U.S.C. 257(a); 37 CFR 1.601(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party other than the patent owner is prohibited from filing papers or otherwise participating in any manner in the supplemental examination proceeding; third-party petitions or papers will not be entered or considered and will be expunged if filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition is statutory. The patent owner may not attempt to circumvent the statute by filing papers on behalf of a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized but defective papers may be expunged
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed that are authorized but defective (e.g., not signed or fail to meet filing date requirements) may be expunged from the official file by marking them 'non-public' and 'closed' so they do not appear in the public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such expunged papers may be refiled appropriately during any resulting ex parte reexamination proceeding; the date of later submission will be the filing date of that paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendments permitted in supplemental examination (37 CFR 1.620(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may be filed in a supplemental examination proceeding; amendments are not 'information believed to be relevant to the patent' and are unauthorized papers that will be expunged if filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners may submit a statutory disclaimer under 35 U.S.C. 253 and 37 CFR 1.321(a) prior to filing a request, or may file a reissue application if they wish to amend patent claims instead of requesting supplemental examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews prohibited in supplemental examination (37 CFR 1.620(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are prohibited in a supplemental examination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition assists processing within the three-month statutory period. Telephone calls to confirm receipt of a request or to discuss general procedural questions are not considered interviews. Interviews in any ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 are governed by ex parte reexamination regulations (e.g., 37 CFR 1.560).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month statutory decision period (SNQ determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months after the filing date of a request for supplemental examination, the Office will determine whether a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) affecting any claim is raised by any of the items of information properly presented in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination will generally be limited to review of the items identified in the request as applied to the identified claims, will be based on the claims in effect at the time of determination, and will become part of the official patent record. The examiner should take up a request about six weeks after filing; if the three-month period ends on a weekend or federal holiday, the certificate should issue by the preceding business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for determining SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard for determining whether an item of information raises a SNQ is the same as set forth in MPEP § 2242 for ex parte reexaminations: whether there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the item important in determining patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination is generally limited to the items of information identified in the request with respect to the identified claims. The supplemental examination certificate containing the determination becomes part of the official record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination limited to identified items and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination will generally be limited to the item(s) of information identified in the request as applied to the identified claim(s) of the patent; if the patent owner wants consideration of an item with respect to multiple claims, each claim must be identified and explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner fails to request consideration of certain claims in view of an item of information, the owner is not entitled to a determination for that item with respect to those claims. The determination is based on claims in effect at time of determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of co-pending litigation and notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners should consider provisions of 35 U.S.C. 257(c)(1) and 257(c)(2) regarding the effect of supplemental examination on pending litigation; the Office takes no position on the issue. The patent owner must promptly notify the Office of any federal court decision involving the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners may wish to consider timing of filing supplemental examination requests in light of pending litigation; the Office's role is limited and does not comment on litigation effects.
